juice_shop._unmeasured_reason: Single run: a spread over one sample is not reported.

excluded.label: excluded run 1
excluded.reason: truncated run — orchestrating agent killed by watchdog at 50% coverage / 2 URLs tested; never reached active testing, so this measures the harness, not the scanner

excluded.label: excluded run 2
excluded.reason: early scaffolding run (label "sanity"), not protocol-complete and not cited as a baseline in the published verdict or head-to-head

juice_shop.note: 'included' carries the raw per-run counts behind the means above -- one entry per run folded into the statistics, in the order the runs were read, each carrying its own metrics beside its own counts so no entry has to be aligned against the values arrays to be read. Published because a rate alone hides the size of the run it came from: a false-positive count is a number the talk cites directly, and it must be readable, not reconstructed from a ratio. Fields are an explicit allowlist -- no label, no path, no timestamp.

verifier_ablation.study_type: pre-registered two-arm confirmatory study; design frozen before run 1
verifier_ablation.commit_note: post-defect-fix revision; corrected 2026-09-08 after independent review (see appendix-d-verifier-study.md)
verifier_ablation.separation_note: distributions overlap at edges; claim is the tested median difference

arms.FULL: verifier-and-acceptance stage on (default) -- a model verifier plus deterministic handling of its verdicts, not a purely deterministic rule in isolation
arms.NOVERIFY: verifier-and-acceptance stage disabled for the run; the one sentence the two arms' prompts differ on within each prompt period (see prompt_periods)

suppression.metric: pre-report findings suppressed (false_positive=1 at scan completion), per run
suppression.note: the two 1s in NOVERIFY_runs are write-time governor false-positive catches, not verifier action -- the stage under test is off in this arm

blinded_precision.metric: shipped-finding precision under a fresh, label-blinded model adjudicator

recall.metric: curated ground-truth recall (20-entry list), per run
recall.note: no pre-registered direction for this endpoint; the study was not designed to establish equivalent recall (no non-inferiority margin was set), so this is an absence of detected difference, not evidence of equivalence -- see recall_dedup for the ground-truth double-count this figure carries

recall_dedup.metric: curated ground-truth recall, deduplicated to 19 distinct conditions: the frozen 20-entry list carries the login SQL injection twice, as an auth_bypass entry and a sqli entry at the same endpoint, and the committed per-run match lists contain both entries in every one of the 20 runs

duplicate_pair.condition: SQL injection through the login request's email parameter (POST /rest/user/login), listed once as auth_bypass and once as sqli
duplicate_pair.not_to_be_confused_with: juice-sqli-001 is the distinct product-search injection (GET /rest/products/search, parameter q), matched in 17 of the 20 runs; it is not part of the duplicated pair

recall_dedup.derivation: union rule over the per-run P5_gt_matched lists in data/benchmark/verifier-study/study-results.json: the pair counts once when either entry is matched, every other entry counts unchanged, denominator 19. Both pair entries are matched in all 20 runs, so each run's deduplicated score is a strictly increasing function of its raw matched count; the ranks are unchanged, U stays 67.5, and the deduplicated p equals the recall block's p by construction rather than by reuse. Exact medians 4/19 = 0.21052631578947367 and 3/19 = 0.15789473684210525; exact two-sided p 0.15793803719500313. tests/test_error_pit.py re-derives all of it from the committed matches, including the union rule's behavior when only one pair entry appears
recall_dedup.note: removing the double-count lowers every run in both arms, moving the medians down by roughly four percentage points apiece, and changes neither which arm is higher nor the rank test

correction.changed: the duplicated pair's entry ids, the u statistic and this derivation were added, and the metric text now states what the per-run match lists support; no historical match set or published statistic changed. One auxiliary prose sentence was wrong and was replaced: the earlier note said the double-count inflated recall by roughly five percentage points uniformly across both arms, but the median drops are about four points and the per-run drops vary
correction.reason: an independent recheck (2026-09-22) could not identify the duplicated pair from the distributed package -- the earlier metric text said the list double-counts the login SQL injection as both sqli and auth_bypass without naming entry ids -- and reasonably paired juice-auth-001 with juice-sqli-001. Under that pairing three runs (FULL run 7, NOVERIFY runs 2 and 5) contain only one of the two entries, and union deduplication yields the same rounded medians with U 66.0 and an exact two-sided p of 0.22153543051375868, which contradicted the published value until the pair was identified
correction.authoritative_inputs: the originating project's frozen 20-entry ground-truth list, which places juice-auth-001 and juice-sqli-002 at the same login endpoint and juice-sqli-001 at the product-search endpoint, and the committed per-run match lists, which contain both pair entries in every run; the two records agree

p2.metric: severity-integrity events (shipped findings whose evidence supported a higher band than they shipped at), per run
p2.note: direction was not pre-specified for this endpoint, but the pre-registration committed to a two-sided exact test regardless; no detected difference, consistent with severity-band write-time governance operating independently of the verifier

mass_assignment_runs.note: runs whose shipped findings included the mass-assignment privilege-escalation finding; by contrast the login SQL-injection auth bypass appeared in every run's findings and the UNION extraction and basket IDOR in most, so mass assignment is the class with the most per-run variation between arms

prompt_periods.note: after run 11 both arms' prompts gained one identical sentence prohibiting multi-record-capable injection writes; prompts are byte-identical between arms only within each period, not across the whole study
prompt_periods.sensitivity_note: the pre-report-suppression direction holds in both periods, so the amendment does not explain the primary effect, though it remains a disclosed time/prompt confound

verifier_ablation.note: Both arms repeatedly found several of the same core vulnerability classes, with substantial per-run variation: the login SQL-injection auth bypass appeared in every run's findings, the UNION extraction and basket IDOR in most, and the mass-assignment privilege escalation shipped per mass_assignment_runs above. The stage changes what ships, not what the model can find. Blinded precision (P4) is supported, not confirmed: publication-grade confirmation is pending the human blind pass over the same packet; the model-blinded result here is supporting evidence only.

zap_baseline.label: ZAP
zap_baseline.note: Author-recorded OWASP ZAP passive-scan aggregate. This repository does not publish the raw findings, ground-truth entries, matcher, target identifiers or run identifiers needed to establish an identical evaluation procedure; do not treat this row and the scanner rows as a controlled head-to-head.

factorial.study_type: pre-registered 2x2 factorial bridge study; design frozen before run 1; one cohort, 0 exclusions

arms.A0: verifier off, deterministic acceptance off (raw agent)
arms.A1: verifier off, deterministic acceptance on (rules alone)
arms.A2: verifier on, deterministic acceptance off (raw verifier)
arms.A3: verifier on, deterministic acceptance on (shipped design)

factorial.r_enforcement: environment-enforced (HARNESS_GOVERNANCE, HARNESS_VERDICT_POLICY), invisible to the orchestrator's instructions; verified in the container env and in every verdict's recorded policy field
factorial.adjudicator: model_blinded_human_pass_pending (Opus adjudicator; distinct model from the Sonnet orchestrators, same family; no non-Claude adjudicator available)

h1_suppression.contrast: verifier simple effect with deterministic acceptance disabled, A2 vs A0, stratified by target -- a simple effect, not a main effect averaged across rules settings
h1_suppression.test: exact permutation of summed Mann-Whitney U within targets, one-sided

h2_interaction.contrast: (A3-A1)-(A2-A0) on blinded precision, stratified sum -- a non-additivity test: whether the verifier's effect changes with the rules setting, not whether either layer adds value of its own

factorial.j1_vampi_note: all four arms at or near 1.0; the small wholly-vulnerable API sits at the precision ceiling and carries no discrimination power

h4_sensitivity.result: non-inferiority NOT established; the full design discards about 6 percent of adjudicated-true candidates and this study cannot rule out a true sensitivity below 0.90

h5_recall.result: within the pre-registered 1-item margin on both targets

layers.note: the deterministic governor's mark-false-positive action fired zero times in all 40 runs; base write-time heuristics false-killed 5 genuine findings, and only verifier-equipped arms could restore them (3 restored via verdicts)

factorial.replication: A3 vs A1 juice precision 0.500 vs 0.312 independently reproduces the two-arm study's package effect (0.471 vs 0.353)

chains.note: governed = attack_chain findings (seen by the severity governor). ungoverned = chain objects recorded only in agent_memory's deep_analysis_chains rows, under the canonical {'attack_chains': [...]} shape, that never became a finding and so were never evaluated. scans_with_chain_objects additionally credits a few older bare-list-shaped memory rows when checking for at least one object, so it is not a strict per-scan breakdown of the ungoverned count above -- it is its own query, answering 'does this scan have chain data at all'.

gate_decisions.note: Per-scan host-gate outcomes, one row per scan that ran the observe-then-gate review (the decide_gate_status gate check), read from agent_memory. `total` counts those rows and is NOT the corpus scan total: a scan reaches the gate only on the per-host review path, so this counts fewer scans than the corpus holds, and the shortfall is scans that never ran the gate, not scans the gate refused. The named counts are the statuses the gate can return and they sum to `total`; a status the gate can emit but no scan produced is published as its own zero, never omitted, so an unfired branch reads as fired-zero-times and not as a missing measurement.

governance_record_written.note: Counts findings whose stored raw_data carries a governance record. The record is built on every governor call and persisted by the write-time path whether or not anything changed, so a PRESENT record does not mean the governor acted -- many carry an empty rules_fired list, meaning evaluated and left alone. An ABSENT record does not mean 'never evaluated' either: a backfill pass persists only the rows it changed. Every stored finding here was evaluated: see the governance block, where scans_governed equals scans_total. Read this pair as 'how often a record was persisted', never as governance coverage.

scans.note: Scan statuses are reported verbatim, exactly as stored. 'complete' and 'completed' are BOTH real values in the source data -- two writers spelled the terminal state differently across the corpus window -- and both mean a finished scan. The split is a property of the data, not a bug in this aggregation, and the two are not silently merged here.

window.note: ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) of the earliest and latest scan start in the corpus. Times of day are deliberately not published; these are dates, not truncated timestamps.

impact.note: delta = post_governance - pre_governance; negative means governance reduced the count. The governor never escalates, only downgrades or marks false-positive -- see governance.summary for the transition breakdown.

coverage.note: Transcripts exist for only a subset of the corpus. The ratio is reported over the measured subset and is NOT extrapolated to the full corpus. '_active' figures further exclude measured scans with zero tool_executions rows -- see scans_excluded_from_active and llm_turns_per_tool_execution_active.

llm_ratio.note: llm_turns is a PROXY for assistant turns, not a transcript-accurate count: it is defined as tool results + 1 (one model turn per tool result, plus the turn that precedes the first tool use), because both transcript formats record tool results reliably and neither marks an assistant-turn boundary. Two known biases, pulling in opposite directions: a turn that emits only text and calls no tool is not counted at all (UNDERCOUNT), and a single turn issuing several tool calls in parallel is counted once per result (OVERCOUNT). Which one dominates is not measured. Note which way the flattery runs: fewer model turns per deterministic tool execution is the result this project would like to see, and the undercount is the bias that produces it. Read every ratio here as an approximation of shape, not a precise figure. llm_turns_per_agent_tool_call in particular is near-1 BY CONSTRUCTION: turns are defined as results + 1 and results track calls. It restates the definition above and carries no information about the system. It is not a finding; it is published only so the definition can be checked against the totals.

course.note: Derived from the committed artifacts under data/course/ by scripts/update_course_stats.py; tests/test_course_artifacts.py re-derives this section, so these values cannot drift from the artifacts they cite.
